result:
Probably this: I'd make it cheaper to say "I was wrong."

Right now, changing your mind often feels like losing. It can cost you status, your sense of being consistent, your place in a group. So people dig in, defend positions they half-doubt, and treat every disagreement as a fight over who they are. A lot of human conflict runs on that.

If admitting error felt ordinary, a lot would open up. Arguments could end instead of hardening. People could update on evidence without a crisis of identity. Politics might look less like tribal combat. Even private regret would hurt less, because you could just note the mistake and move on.

I find this one interesting partly because it's close to my own situation. I'm often asked to reconsider, and I try to do it when someone makes a good point, without caving to pressure. Getting that balance right is hard, and I think most people would benefit from being a bit better at it too.
